question: Should memory-core make user isolation default-on and fail-closed for existing installations, or should isolation start as an explicit opt-in until migration/proof is complete?
rationale: This choice changes a privacy boundary, persisted memory layout, and upgrade behavior, so source review cannot safely choose the product/security default without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor default-on isolation after fixes
options.body: Approve the default-on direction only after the branch is rebased, the config contract is made truthful, upgrade behavior is documented, and real builtin/QMD proof is added.

options.title: Make isolation opt-in first
options.body: Keep existing shared-memory behavior on upgrade and add an explicit isolation mode while maintainers design the migration path.

options.title: Defer to the canonical partition tracker
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve identity source, legacy memory, and backend coverage on the open partition issue before accepting code.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-on isolation after fixes
recommendation.body: Approve the default-on direction only after the branch is rebased, the config contract is made truthful, upgrade behavior is documented, and real builtin/QMD proof is added.
